passage:
Supervisor's note, week 6, Akash (intern)
Akash checks every figure three or four times before sending it. On Tuesday that caught a decimal error in the vendor invoice that would have cost us badly. I thanked him in front of the team.
The same habit has a cost. When I asked for a volunteer to try the new warehouse software pilot, Akash looked down. Later he told me, 'What if it doesn't work and I've wasted two weeks?' Kiran took it instead, and it is going well.
What I did next: I asked Akash to list what could actually go wrong with the pilot and how bad each would be. His list was short and mostly fixable. He said, 'It's not really risky, is it? I was just scared.' He has joined the pilot for the second phase.
Reena

qa.q: What error did Akash's checking catch on Tuesday?
qa.a: A decimal error in the vendor invoice.

qa.q: What was Akash worried about when he looked down at the request for a volunteer?
qa.a: He worried the pilot might not work and that he would have wasted two weeks.

qa.q: What turning point helped Akash join the pilot?
qa.a: Listing what could go wrong and how bad each would be showed a short, fixable list, so Akash saw that fear, not judgment, had been deciding.

qa.q: How might Kiran see the pilot compared with how Akash first saw it?
qa.a: Kiran seems to have seen it as a chance to try something new, while Akash first saw mainly the risk of wasted time.

grounding: Shows a cautious young adult whose checking guards against loss but whose fear made him miss a chance, until he weighs the real risks.

passage:
Thursday night
Gautam messaged again: the mountaineering institute has two seats left in the basic course, and he wants us to take them together. I've read the syllabus four times. Checked the reviews, the weather, the refund rules, the old accident records.
Part of this is good sense. I'm the one who noticed last year that the cheap trekking agency Gautam liked had no licence. Caution saved us then.
But tonight I made myself be honest. The institute is licensed. The instructors are experienced. The refund is fair. There's no fact left that says no. It's only the tight feeling in my chest saying no.
I don't want fear to be the one making my choices. I'm going to fill in the form tomorrow before lunch, before I talk myself out of it.
Dolma

qa.q: What did Dolma notice last year about the trekking agency Gautam liked?
qa.a: That the cheap trekking agency had no licence.

qa.q: What does Dolma realise is really saying no tonight?
qa.a: Dolma realises no fact says no anymore; only the tight feeling in Dolma's chest, fear, is holding back.

qa.q: What choice does Dolma make, and why before lunch?
qa.a: Dolma decides to fill in the form tomorrow before lunch, early enough that fear can't talk Dolma out of a choice the facts support.

qa.q: How might Gautam feel when Dolma finally agrees?
qa.a: Gautam would likely feel happy and relieved, and may trust Dolma's careful checking even more after it spotted the unlicensed agency.

grounding: Shows a cautious young adult whose checking protects against real risks, and who notices when fear rather than judgment is deciding.

passage: Urmila's plan was simple: a Sunday momo stall outside the Ludhiana college gate. She needed one partner. Gurpreet read her cost sheet three times, then looked up every rule about street stalls, then asked his uncle, then read the sheet again. "What if it rains? What if nobody comes?" By the time he'd finished checking, Urmila had partnered with someone else. The stall sold out in two hours on its first Sunday. Gurpreet watched from across the road, eating a momo he'd paid for, and felt something between relief and regret. Had he been careful, or just afraid? He honestly couldn't tell.

qa.q: How long did the stall take to sell out on its first Sunday?
qa.a: Two hours.

qa.q: What did Gurpreet feel watching the stall from across the road?
qa.a: A mix of relief and regret, unsure whether he had been careful or afraid.

qa.q: What could Gurpreet ask himself next time to tell judgement from fear?
qa.a: Whether each worry is backed by facts he has checked, or whether it is fear stopping him after the facts are clear.

qa.q: How might Urmila have felt waiting for Gurpreet's answer?
qa.a: Urmila was probably impatient and a little disappointed, so she found another partner.

grounding: Shows a cautious young adult who checks and rechecks, then misses a chance and wonders whether fear decided.

passage:
"The exchange semester in Seoul, Vidya! Deadline's Friday."
"I saw it, Sabina." Vidya didn't look up from her notes. "I read the whole page. Twice. And the reviews from last year's students. And the visa rules."
"And?"
"And my credits might not transfer. And the hostel reviews are mixed. And I don't speak Korean."
"Nobody speaks Korean. That's the point."
"What if I hate it and can't come back?"
Sabina sat on the bed. "Okay. Is that a real reason, or is that fear talking?"
Vidya was quiet. "I checked the credit thing with the office. They said it's fine."
"So?"
"So it's mostly fear." Vidya chewed her pen. "Maybe I'll fill in the form. Just fill it in."

qa.q: What did the office say about the credits?
qa.a: They said it's fine.

qa.q: What was Vidya feeling about the exchange semester?
qa.a: She felt anxious and afraid of hating it, even after checking the facts.

qa.q: What question from Sabina helped Vidya?
qa.a: Whether her reasons were real or fear talking, which helped her see the facts were already checked.

qa.q: How does Sabina see Vidya's worries?
qa.a: Sabina sees them as mostly fear and gently pushes Vidya not to miss the chance.

grounding: Illustrates a cautious young adult who checks facts many times and learns to tell judgement from fear.

passage: I'm Jaya, twenty-two, and I've never regretted being careful. When my classmates put their savings into some online trading scheme last year, I read everything, asked my uncle, who's an accountant, and stayed out. Half of them lost money. I felt vindicated. But there's another story. My friend Dolma asked me to join her trekking-guide course in Sikkim: three weeks, a bit risky, unpaid. I made a list of forty things that could go wrong. I said no. She came back glowing, with a job offer. I keep asking myself: did my judgement decide that, or did fear? With the trading, it was judgement. With the trek, I think it was fear.

qa.q: Who did Jaya ask about the trading scheme?
qa.a: Jaya's uncle, who's an accountant.

qa.q: How did Jaya feel about staying out of the trading scheme?
qa.a: Jaya felt vindicated when half the classmates lost money.

qa.q: What could Jaya do differently the next time a chance like the trek comes up?
qa.a: Check the real facts, as with the trading, and ask whether the no is judgement or fear before deciding.

qa.q: How did Dolma experience the trek course?
qa.a: Dolma came back glowing, with a job offer.

grounding: Shows a cautious young adult whose care protected against loss once but may have cost a chance when fear decided.

passage:
Internship supervisor's note, Darshan, week eight.
Darshan's research is meticulous. He checks every figure three times, and his reports have zero errors. On Monday he spotted a mistake in a supplier invoice that saved us real trouble.
But on Thursday, when I offered him the chance to pitch his own idea for the new recycling project to the director, he said, "I'd rather not. It hasn't been tried before." His co-intern, Pallavi, pitched instead, with half the preparation.
Afterwards he admitted, "I was scared of getting it wrong in front of everyone." His idea, I think, was better.
What I did next: I told him his caution is a strength, and asked him to check whether fear or facts had made the call. Next week he will present his idea to me alone first, then decide about the director.

qa.q: What did Darshan spot in the supplier invoice?
qa.a: A mistake that saved them real trouble.

qa.q: What was Darshan feeling when he turned down the pitch?
qa.a: He was scared of getting it wrong in front of everyone, so he chose the familiar, safe path.

qa.q: What did the supervisor suggest to help Darshan tell judgment from fear?
qa.a: To ask whether fear or facts made the call, and to present the idea to the supervisor alone first before deciding about the director.

qa.q: How might Pallavi's pitch look from Darshan's side?
qa.a: Seeing Pallavi pitch with half the preparation may leave Darshan feeling regret about the missed chance, since his idea may have been better.

grounding: Shows a supervisor noting a cautious young adult whose checking guards against loss, but whose fear causes him to miss a chance.
